en: So we already see the first 2
HTMX attributes in action and how we can use
them to send a request declaratively without
writing any JavaScript code and how we can
control
where exactly in the element that sent the
request the response content will be
rendered.
But what if we actually don't wanna render
the content in the button or instead of the
button at all?
What if we wanna render it somewhere else,
maybe below the button?
Well, you can of course also configure that
because HTMX offers all those attributes
here to allow you to essentially configure
it in any way you need
without writing JavaScript code.
And the configuration and extra attribute we
need here is hx-target.
And by the way, the order of these
attributes here is not important.
I tend to start with the
request attributes, hx-get and some others,
which I'll show you later, but it's not
important.
hx-target is important here though if we
wanna render the response content somewhere
else and not inside or instead of this
button.
Because hx-target now takes a CSS selector
as a value and that selector selects any
element on the page, so any element in the
currently rendered DOM
into which the response data will be
rendered.
And then hx-swap will still define
if the response content will be rendered
instead of the selected element or inside of
the selected element or inside in front of
existing elements and so on.
And here I wanna target the entire main
element and then render the response content
at the end of that element. So after the
existing content, after this paragraph and
this button.
So therefore I now need the CSS selector for
the main element And here I can of course
simply select that by its tag name, so I can
just write main here.
And this will now select the main element.
By the way, if you had a target here that's
matched by multiple elements,
if I would, for example, select a paragraph
and I had multiple paragraphs on the page,
then it would target the first matching
element, not all of them.
But here, of course, I wanna select the main
element and I only have one main element
anyways,
and therefore I'll target that.
However, now I don't wanna swap the entire
element because if I would leave it like
this and I would save that
and I would reload,
you would see that clicking the Learn More
button would now actually replace the entire
main element. With the rendered content.
That might be what you want, but it's
actually not what I want here.
Instead, I wanna render this response
content inside of the main element after the
existing content.
Now, if we take another look at the hx-swap
documentation,
we can see that
before-end might be the setting we want here
because that will insert the response after
the last child of the target element.
And that's exactly what we want here. We
wanna persist the elements, we wanna keep
them, but then we wanna add the response
data after those elements.
And therefore here it's before
end that I want as a setting here.
And I'll now split that across multiple
lines to make it a bit easier to read, but
that's just for for cosmetic reasons.
With that setting in place, if you save
everything again and you reload, if you
click the button, you see now the button and
this text here is kept, but then the list is
added after these elements. And that's
exactly the behavior I wanted here.
